chunks: From him, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: In what distance do I shorten the salat (prayer)? He said: In one barīd. Do you not see that the people of Makkah, when they go out to ʿArafah, shortening is incumbent upon them?

key_terms.أَهْلَ مَكَّةَ: the people of Makkah, cited here as an example
key_terms.أُقَصِّرُ: I shorten; referring here to shortening the salat (prayer) while traveling
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the salat (prayer) that is shortened in travel
key_terms.بَرِيدٍ: a barīd; a measured travel distance used in legal rulings
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: ʿArafah, the well-known location to which pilgrims travel

ai.seo_question: At what travel distance does one shorten the salat (prayer) according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling for shortening the salat (prayer) during travel, specifying that it applies at a distance of one barīd. The Imam عليه السلام supports the ruling by citing the practice of the people of Makkah when they travel to ʿArafah.
